questions.q: How does Brian Tracy suggest using a daily commute?
a: Listening to audiobooks, courses or language tapes
Catching up on sleep before the workday starts
Planning every meeting for the following week
Calling clients to build stronger relationships
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the hours spent commuting can be turned into learning time with audiobooks, programs or language tapes.

questions.q: What does knowing yourself mean in the summary?
a: Knowing your strengths, weaknesses and best working hours
Knowing which tasks your colleagues dislike most
Knowing how to say no to every extra request
Knowing your salary compared with the market rate
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines self-awareness as knowing what you are and are not good at, plus the time of day when you are most productive.

questions.q: What did Charlie Munger do with the hour he sold himself as a client?
a: He worked on his own projects instead of billing others
He studied law so he could charge higher fees
He rested so he could work longer hours later
He taught young lawyers for a small fee
questions.why: Lesson 3 recounts Munger deciding his most important client was himself and using a paid hour each day for his own ventures.

questions.q: What share of emotions does the summary say comes from self-talk?
a: 95 percent
50 percent
75 percent
10 percent
questions.why: Lesson 2 states that 95 percent of emotions stem from our internal self-talk.

questions.q: How does Tracy recommend reserving time for personal goals?
a: Block chunks of time on your calendar and keep them
Wait for a free evening and work as long as possible
Work on them only after every other task is finished
Delegate them to someone with more spare time
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends blocking time in chunks on the calendar and using those appointments to advance personal goals.
